6. **Treasurer:** The Treasurer shall be responsible for:
   a. Maintaining proper books of account for all funds of the Committee;
   b. Preparing a financial report for each regular meeting;
   c. Preparing the annual budget and the audited financial statements for the Annual General Meeting; and
   d. Making all payments authorised by the Committee, with the signature of the Chairperson or Vice-Chairperson as co-signatory.

---

**ARTICLE IV: MEETINGS**

1. **Regular Meetings:** The Committee shall meet at least once every calendar month for the transaction of ordinary business. The exact date, time, and venue of each regular meeting shall be fixed by the Committee at the preceding meeting, and the Secretary shall notify all members in writing or by electronic means not less than seven (7) days in advance.

2. **Special Meetings:** A special meeting may be convened at any time by the Chairperson, or upon the written request of not fewer than one-third (1/3) of the members. The notice for a special meeting shall state the specific business to be transacted, and no other business shall be discussed at that meeting.

3. **Quorum:** The quorum for any meeting shall be one-half (1/2) of the total membership, excluding the Chairperson unless the Chairperson is counted to make up the required number. No business shall be transacted at any meeting unless a quorum is present.

4. **Voting:** Each member present shall have one (1) vote. All questions shall be decided by a simple majority of votes cast, except where this Constitution provides otherwise. The Chairperson shall have a casting vote in addition to his or her ordinary vote.

5. **Minutes:** The minutes of each meeting shall be recorded by the Secretary and shall be confirmed at the next meeting. Once confirmed, the minutes shall be signed by the Chairperson and kept in a bound minute book or secure electronic repository.

6. **Proxy and Absence:** No member may vote by proxy. A member who is unable to attend a meeting shall tender an apology to the Secretary prior to the meeting, which shall be recorded.

---

**ARTICLE V: DECISION-MAKING AND DELEGATION**

1. The Committee may delegate specific duties to sub-committees or to individual officers, provided that any such delegation is recorded in the minutes and reported to the Committee.

2. A sub-committee shall have no power to incur expenditure on behalf of the Committee except as expressly authorised by the Committee.

3. Urgent decisions requiring action between meetings may be made by the Chairperson in consultation with the Secretary and Treasurer, and shall be reported to the Committee at the next regular meeting.

---

**ARTICLE VI: FINANCIAL OVERSIGHT**

1. The Committee shall maintain a bank account in the name of the Serangoon Hawker Centre Management Committee, and all funds received shall be deposited therein without delay.

2. All cheques or electronic transfers shall be signed or authorised by any two (2) of the following: Chairperson, Treasurer, and Secretary.

3. The Treasurer shall present a financial report at every regular meeting, showing receipts and expenditures since the previous report.

4. The accounts of the Committee shall be audited annually by an independent auditor appointed at the Annual General Meeting, and the audited accounts shall be presented to the members.

5. **Serangoon Hawker Centre Management Committee meeting_frequency monthly. Record status: current.** The regular monthly meeting shall include a standing item for the review of financial statements and any outstanding receivables or payables.

---

**ARTICLE VII: ANNUAL GENERAL MEETING**

1.
**CONSTITUTION AND STANDING ORDERS OF THE SERANGONG HAWKER CENTRE MANAGEMENT COMMITTEE**

*(Adopted 2022; amendments noted in footnotes)*

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

| Article | Title |
|---------|-------|
| I | Name and Objectives |
| II | Membership and Eligibility |
| III | Officers and Duties |
| IV | Meetings and Procedure |
| V | Decision-Making and Delegation |
| VI | Financial Oversight |
| VII | Annual General Meeting |
| VIII | Sub-Committees |
| IX | Financial Year, Budget, and Audit |
| X | Amendments |
| XI | Dissolution |

---

**ARTICLE VIII: SUB-COMMITTEES**

1. The Committee shall establish the following standing sub-committees, each reporting to the Committee at every regular meeting:

a. Finance Sub-Committee;
   b. Operations Sub-Committee; and
   c. Hygiene Inspection Sub-Committee.

2. Each sub-committee shall consist of not fewer than three (3) and not more than five (5) members, at least one of whom shall be a member of the Committee. The Chairperson of each sub-committee shall be appointed by the Committee and shall be a Committee member.

3. The terms of reference of each sub-committee are set out below and may be amended by the Committee from time to time, provided that any amendment is recorded in the minutes.

4. **Finance Sub-Committee**

a. The Finance Sub-Committee shall assist the Treasurer in the preparation of the annual budget, the monitoring of receipts and expenditures, and the review of financial reports prior to their presentation to the Committee.

b. The Finance Sub-Committee shall review all proposals for expenditure exceeding five hundred dollars ($500) and shall make recommendations to the Committee.

c. The Finance Sub-Committee shall meet at least once in each quarter and shall maintain a record of its deliberations, which shall be made available to the Committee upon request.

5. **Operations Sub-Committee**

a. The Operations Sub-Committee shall oversee the day-to-day management of the common areas of the hawker centre, including but not limited to cleaning schedules, waste disposal, lighting, and the upkeep of shared facilities.

b. The Operations Sub-Committee shall liaise with the relevant government agencies and service providers on matters relating to the maintenance and repair of the hawker centre.

c. The Operations Sub-Committee shall report any significant operational issue to the Committee within seven (7) days of its occurrence.

6. **Hygiene Inspection Sub-Committee**

a. The Hygiene Inspection Sub-Committee shall conduct inspections of stalls and common areas to ensure compliance with the prevailing hygiene standards and regulations.

b. The Hygiene Inspection Sub-Committee shall maintain inspection records and shall submit a summary of findings to the Committee at each regular meeting.

c. The Hygiene Inspection Sub-Committee shall, upon identifying a serious breach of hygiene standards, immediately inform the Chairperson and the relevant authority.

7. Sub-committees shall have no power to bind the Committee or to incur expenditure except as expressly authorised under Article V, Clause 2.

8. Each sub-committee shall stand dissolved upon the conclusion of each Annual General Meeting and shall be reconstituted by the newly elected Committee at its first meeting.

---

**ARTICLE IX: FINANCIAL YEAR, BUDGET, AND AUDIT**

1. The financial year of the Committee shall commence on 1 April and end on 31 March of the following year.
**ARTICLE X: DISPUTE RESOLUTION**

1. Any dispute arising between members of the Committee, or between the Committee and any stallholder, contractor, or member of the public, shall in the first instance be referred to the Chairperson for informal mediation.

2. Where the Chairperson is a party to the dispute, or where the Chairperson is unable or unwilling to act, the Vice-Chairperson shall conduct the mediation.

3. If informal mediation under Clauses 1 and 2 fails to resolve the dispute within fourteen (14) days, the dispute shall be referred to a Dispute Resolution Panel constituted as follows:
   a. The Chairperson shall appoint one (1) member of the Committee who is not a party to the dispute.
   b. The parties to the dispute shall each appoint one (1) person, who need not be a member of the Committee.
   c. The three (3) persons so appointed shall elect a fourth person to chair the Panel.

4. The Dispute Resolution Panel shall have the power to:
   a. Call for documents and records relevant to the dispute;
   b. Interview witnesses, provided that the parties are given an opportunity to be present and to respond;
   c. Recommend a settlement, which shall be put to the parties in writing.

5. A recommendation of the Dispute Resolution Panel shall not be binding on the parties unless both parties accept it in writing.

6. Nothing in this Article shall prevent any party from seeking redress through the Small Claims Tribunals, the Community Mediation Centre, or any other lawful means, at any stage of the dispute.

7. The costs of any mediation or Dispute Resolution Panel proceeding shall be borne equally by the parties, unless the Panel recommends otherwise and both parties agree.

8. The Committee shall maintain a confidential register of disputes referred under this Article, recording the nature of the dispute, the steps taken, and the outcome. The register shall be made available to the external auditors upon request but shall not be disclosed to the general public.

**ARTICLE XI: DISSOLUTION**

1. The Committee may be dissolved by a resolution passed by a two-thirds (2/3) majority of the members present and voting at an Extraordinary General Meeting, provided that:
   a. At least twenty-one (21) days' notice of the meeting and of the proposed resolution has been given in writing to all members;
   b. A quorum of at least half (1/2) of the members is present at the meeting.

2. Upon the passing of a resolution to dissolve, the Committee shall:
   a. Cease to incur any further expenditure, except as necessary for the winding-up of its affairs;
   b. Appoint a liquidator, who may be a member of the Committee or an external person;
   c. Prepare a final statement of accounts as at the date of dissolution.

3. The liquidator shall:
   a. Settle all outstanding debts and liabilities of the Committee;
   b. Dispose of any remaining assets, which shall be donated to a charitable organisation or to the Town Council for the benefit of the hawker centre, as the dissolution resolution may direct;
   c. Submit a final report and statement of accounts to the Town Council within three (3) months of the date of dissolution.

4. Upon the completion of the winding-up, the Committee shall be deemed dissolved and shall cease to exist.

5. Any surplus funds remaining after the settlement of debts and liabilities shall not be distributed among the members but shall be applied in accordance with Clause 3(b).

*Inspection of 27 January 2023 (Full)*
- Overall score: 88/100
- Key finding: The recycling bins at the loading bay were overflowing on the day of inspection. The bin collection schedule had been changed by the town council, and CleanCo had not been notified.
- Corrective action: CleanCo arranged an extra collection on 30 January. The HIU has since requested that the town council copy CleanCo on any schedule changes.
- Recommendation: Review the waste collection contract to include a clause on notification of external schedule changes.

*Spot checks of 6 February and 21 February 2023*
- Both checks scored above 90/100. No significant findings. Minor issues (e.g., a missing soap dispenser lid) were rectified within 24 hours.

**3. Quarterly Inspection Schedule**

Under the Operations Sub-committee policy, the Hygiene Inspection Unit inspection_frequency quarterly. Record status: current. This means that the HIU is required to complete a full inspection of all designated areas once per quarter, in addition to any spot checks deemed necessary.

Each quarterly inspection will cover all areas listed in the HIU scope, with a minimum of 20 inspection points per area. The HIU will report the results to the Management Committee in the month following the inspection window.

**4. Findings from the Q1 Inspection (27 January 2023)**

**ARTICLE IV: MEETINGS**

1. **Regular Meetings:** The Committee shall meet at least once every calendar month for the transaction of ordinary business. The exact date, time, and venue of each regular meeting shall be fixed by the Committee at the preceding meeting, and the Secretary shall notify all members in writing or by electronic means not less than seven (7) days in advance.

2. **Special Meetings:** A special meeting may be convened at any time by the Chairperson, or upon the written request of not fewer than one-third (1/3) of the members. The notice for a special meeting shall state the specific business to be transacted, and no other business shall be discussed at that meeting.

3. **Quorum:** The quorum for any meeting shall be one-half (1/2) of the total membership, excluding the Chairperson unless the Chairperson is counted to make up the required number. No business shall be transacted at any meeting unless a quorum is present.

4. **Voting:** Each member present shall have one (1) vote. All questions shall be decided by a simple majority of votes cast, except where this Constitution provides otherwise. The Chairperson shall have a casting vote in addition to his or her ordinary vote.

5. **Minutes:** The minutes of each meeting shall be recorded by the Secretary and shall be confirmed at the next meeting. Once confirmed, the minutes shall be signed by the Chairperson and kept in a bound minute book or secure electronic repository.

6. **Proxy and Absence:** No member may vote by proxy. A member who is unable to attend a meeting shall tender an apology to the Secretary prior to the meeting, which shall be recorded.

---

1. The Committee may delegate specific duties to sub-committees or to individual officers, provided that any such delegation is recorded in the minutes and reported to the Committee.

2. A sub-committee shall have no power to incur expenditure on behalf of the Committee except as expressly authorised by the Committee.

3. Urgent decisions requiring action between meetings may be made by the Chairperson in consultation with the Secretary and Treasurer, and shall be reported to the Committee at the next regular meeting.

4. The accounts of the Committee shall be audited annually by an independent auditor appointed at the Annual General Meeting, and the audited accounts shall be presented to the members.

---

**ARTICLE VIII: SUB-COMMITTEES**

1. The Committee shall establish the following standing sub-committees, each reporting to the Committee at every regular meeting:

a. Finance Sub-Committee;
   b. Operations Sub-Committee; and
   c. Hygiene Inspection Sub-Committee.

2. Each sub-committee shall consist of not fewer than three (3) and not more than five (5) members, at least one of whom shall be a member of the Committee. The Chairperson of each sub-committee shall be appointed by the Committee and shall be a Committee member.

3. The terms of reference of each sub-committee are set out below and may be amended by the Committee from time to time, provided that any amendment is recorded in the minutes.

4. **Finance Sub-Committee**

a. The Finance Sub-Committee shall assist the Treasurer in the preparation of the annual budget, the monitoring of receipts and expenditures, and the review of financial reports prior to their presentation to the Committee.

b. The Finance Sub-Committee shall review all proposals for expenditure exceeding five hundred dollars ($500) and shall make recommendations to the Committee.

c. The Finance Sub-Committee shall meet at least once in each quarter and shall maintain a record of its deliberations, which shall be made available to the Committee upon request.

5. **Operations Sub-Committee**

a. The Operations Sub-Committee shall oversee the day-to-day management of the common areas of the hawker centre, including but not limited to cleaning schedules, waste disposal, lighting, and the upkeep of shared facilities.

b. The Operations Sub-Committee shall liaise with the relevant government agencies and service providers on matters relating to the maintenance and repair of the hawker centre.

c. The Operations Sub-Committee shall report any significant operational issue to the Committee within seven (7) days of its occurrence.

6. **Hygiene Inspection Sub-Committee**

a. The Hygiene Inspection Sub-Committee shall conduct inspections of stalls and common areas to ensure compliance with the prevailing hygiene standards and regulations.

b. The Hygiene Inspection Sub-Committee shall maintain inspection records and shall submit a summary of findings to the Committee at each regular meeting.

c. The Hygiene Inspection Sub-Committee shall, upon identifying a serious breach of hygiene standards, immediately inform the Chairperson and the relevant authority.

7. Sub-committees shall have no power to bind the Committee or to incur expenditure except as expressly authorised under Article V, Clause 2.

8. Each sub-committee shall stand dissolved upon the conclusion of each Annual General Meeting and shall be reconstituted by the newly elected Committee at its first meeting.

---

**ARTICLE IX: FINANCIAL YEAR, BUDGET, AND AUDIT**

1. The financial year of the Committee shall commence on 1 April and end on 31 March of the following year.

**ARTICLE X: DISPUTE RESOLUTION**

1. Any dispute arising between members of the Committee, or between the Committee and any stallholder, contractor, or member of the public, shall in the first instance be referred to the Chairperson for informal mediation.

2. Where the Chairperson is a party to the dispute, or where the Chairperson is unable or unwilling to act, the Vice-Chairperson shall conduct the mediation.

3. If informal mediation under Clauses 1 and 2 fails to resolve the dispute within fourteen (14) days, the dispute shall be referred to a Dispute Resolution Panel constituted as follows:
   a. The Chairperson shall appoint one (1) member of the Committee who is not a party to the dispute.
   b. The parties to the dispute shall each appoint one (1) person, who need not be a member of the Committee.
   c. The three (3) persons so appointed shall elect a fourth person to chair the Panel.

4. The Dispute Resolution Panel shall have the power to:
   a. Call for documents and records relevant to the dispute;
   b. Interview witnesses, provided that the parties are given an opportunity to be present and to respond;
   c. Recommend a settlement, which shall be put to the parties in writing.

5. A recommendation of the Dispute Resolution Panel shall not be binding on the parties unless both parties accept it in writing.

6. Nothing in this Article shall prevent any party from seeking redress through the Small Claims Tribunals, the Community Mediation Centre, or any other lawful means, at any stage of the dispute.

7. The costs of any mediation or Dispute Resolution Panel proceeding shall be borne equally by the parties, unless the Panel recommends otherwise and both parties agree.

8. The Committee shall maintain a confidential register of disputes referred under this Article, recording the nature of the dispute, the steps taken, and the outcome. The register shall be made available to the external auditors upon request but shall not be disclosed to the general public.

**ARTICLE XI: DISSOLUTION**

1. The Committee may be dissolved by a resolution passed by a two-thirds (2/3) majority of the members present and voting at an Extraordinary General Meeting, provided that:
   a. At least twenty-one (21) days' notice of the meeting and of the proposed resolution has been given in writing to all members;
   b. A quorum of at least half (1/2) of the members is present at the meeting.

2. Upon the passing of a resolution to dissolve, the Committee shall:
   a. Cease to incur any further expenditure, except as necessary for the winding-up of its affairs;
   b. Appoint a liquidator, who may be a member of the Committee or an external person;
   c. Prepare a final statement of accounts as at the date of dissolution.

3. The liquidator shall:
   a. Settle all outstanding debts and liabilities of the Committee;
   b. Dispose of any remaining assets, which shall be donated to a charitable organisation or to the Town Council for the benefit of the hawker centre, as the dissolution resolution may direct;
   c. Submit a final report and statement of accounts to the Town Council within three (3) months of the date of dissolution.

4. Upon the completion of the winding-up, the Committee shall be deemed dissolved and shall cease to exist.

5. Any surplus funds remaining after the settlement of debts and liabilities shall not be distributed among the members but shall be applied in accordance with Clause 3(b).

**4. PRESENTATION BY GUEST – NATIONAL ENVIRONMENT AGENCY**

The Chair welcomed Mr. Tan Wei Ming, Senior Officer from the National Environment Agency (NEA), who was present at the invitation of the Committee to speak on hygiene standards at the hawker centre.

Mr. Tan began by thanking the Committee for the invitation and acknowledged the centre's generally good track record in past inspections. He noted that NEA conducts regular visits to hawker centres across Singapore, and that the upcoming annual licensing renewal exercise (referred to in the letter dated 28 March 2023) will be tied to a review of each stallholder's compliance history.

He highlighted the following key points:

1. **Food Handler Certificates:** All stallholders and their assistants must possess valid food handler certificates. Mr. Tan reminded the Committee that lapses in this area are the most common reason for licensing delays. He advised the Committee to conduct a quick audit of all stallholders' certificates before the renewal deadline.

2. **Pest Control:** Mr. Tan noted that pest sightings are a recurring issue at many centres. He commended the Committee for obtaining a quotation for quarterly pest control services (see item 8.1 below) and advised that records of such services should be kept for at least one year for inspection purposes.

3. **Cleaning of Common Areas:** He referenced the complaint received regarding the common wash area near the toilet entrance (see item 2.3 above). Mr. Tan stressed that common areas, including wash areas and corridors, are subject to the same cleanliness standards as individual stalls. He recommended that the cleaning supervisor keep a daily log of cleaning activities for the common areas.

4. **Upcoming Inspections:** Mr. Tan informed the Committee that NEA will be conducting a series of inspections at hawker centres in the Serangoon area in the coming months. He could not provide specific dates but advised the Committee to ensure that all areas of the centre, including the rear service corridor and the refuse room, are in order.

**Questions and Answers**

The following questions were raised by Committee members, with responses from Mr. Tan:

**Mr. Goh Boon Kiat (Honorary Treasurer):** Asked whether the recent increase in utility costs would affect the licensing renewal fees.

*Mr. Tan:* Responded that licensing fees are determined by NEA and are not linked to utility costs. He advised the Committee to direct any queries on utility charges to the respective service providers.

**Mdm. Lim Siew Hong (Member):** Asked whether NEA could provide any templates or checklists for self-inspection purposes.

*Mr. Tan:* Confirmed that NEA has published a self-inspection checklist on its website, which stallholders and the Committee can use. He offered to circulate the link to the Secretary after the meeting.

**Mr. Tan Kok Leong (Vice-Chair):** Raised a question regarding the disposal of used cooking oil, noting that some stallholders may not be using licensed collectors.

*Mr. Tan:* Advised that all used cooking oil must be collected by licensed collectors, and that the Committee should maintain a list of licensed collectors for reference. He offered to provide a copy of the list to the Committee.

**Mr. Rajan s/o Krishnan (Member):** Asked about the protocol for handling feedback from the public regarding hygiene issues.

*Mr. Tan:* Explained that all feedback received by NEA is logged and investigated. He encouraged the Committee to address feedback promptly at the centre level, as this would reflect positively in NEA's records.

Our inspections are conducted against the following criteria:

**2. Summary of Recent Inspection Activities (December 2022 – February 2023)**

The HIU conducted two full inspections and three spot checks during the December 2022 to February 2023 period. Findings are summarised below.

*Inspection of 12 December 2022 (Full)*
- Overall score: 82/100
- Key finding: Build-up of grease residue in the corner floor drains of the main kitchen (Area K2). CleanCo had missed this spot on their daily log.
- Corrective action: CleanCo degreased the drains on 14 December. Follow-up check on 15 December confirmed the area was clean.
- Recommendation: Add corner drains to CleanCo’s daily checklist for Area K2.

*Inspection of 9 January 2023 (Spot – Level 3 washrooms)*
- Overall score: 91/100
- Key finding: One hand dryer in the male washroom (Unit 3B) was not functioning. The unit emitted air but no heat.
- Corrective action: Maintenance submitted a work order on 10 January. The dryer was replaced on 13 January.
- Recommendation: Include hand dryer functionality in the monthly maintenance checklist, not just the annual service.

*Inspection of 27 January 2023 (Full)*
- Overall score: 88/100
- Key finding: The recycling bins at the loading bay were overflowing on the day of inspection. The bin collection schedule had been changed by the town council, and CleanCo had not been notified.
- Corrective action: CleanCo arranged an extra collection on 30 January. The HIU has since requested that the town council copy CleanCo on any schedule changes.
- Recommendation: Review the waste collection contract to include a clause on notification of external schedule changes.

*Spot checks of 6 February and 21 February 2023*
- Both checks scored above 90/100. No significant findings. Minor issues (e.g., a missing soap dispenser lid) were rectified within 24 hours.

**3. Quarterly Inspection Schedule**

Under the Operations Sub-committee policy, the Hygiene Inspection Unit inspection_frequency quarterly. Record status: current. This means that the HIU is required to complete a full inspection of all designated areas once per quarter, in addition to any spot checks deemed necessary.

Each quarterly inspection will cover all areas listed in the HIU scope, with a minimum of 20 inspection points per area. The HIU will report the results to the Management Committee in the month following the inspection window.

**4. Findings from the Q1 Inspection (27 January 2023)**

The Q1 inspection was completed on 27 January 2023. A total of 48 inspection points were assessed across 12 areas. The overall score was 88/100.

- Loading Bay (74/100) – due to overflowing recycling bins as noted above

The contractor has requested a 4-week extension due to a delay in the supply of the specified porcelain tiles. The tiles were ordered from Italy and shipment was held up at port for inspection. We have inspected the samples that arrived and they meet spec. The contractor has agreed to work Saturdays (subject to noise restrictions) to make up some of the lost time. Revised completion is 17 Jan 2025, which we have accepted in writing.

**1.2 Carpark Level 2 Resealing (Project OPS-2024-05)**

Resealing works completed on 28 Dec 2024. However, during our walkthrough on 30 Dec we noticed water ponding in two bays near the lift lobby entrance. The contractor (SealRight Pte Ltd) has been asked to return and rectify. They have attributed the ponding to a fall issue rather than the sealant. We are awaiting their written rectification proposal. The defect liability period is 12 months, so no additional cost to the MC. We expect rectification to be done by mid-Jan.

**1.3 Common Corridor Repainting – Block C (Project OPS-2024-07)**

Works completed on 15 Dec 2024. Final invoice received and paid. No outstanding issues. Minor touch-up required on Level 9 stairwell where the painter’s ladder scratched the wall – we have requested the contractor to do this under defect liability. No cost.

**1.4 Roof Waterproofing – Block B (Project OPS-2024-09)**

Tender closed 20 Dec 2024. Three bids received. Evaluation in progress. We will present the tender evaluation report at the next meeting for award. The three bids are within a narrow range and we have no concerns on the budget. We have checked the references of the two lowest bidders – both have done similar work on HDB blocks nearby. Recommendation to award is being prepared.

---

**2. ONGOING MAINTENANCE ISSUES**

**2.1 Lift No. 3 – Block A**

We have received two complaints in December about the lift stopping between floors. The lift contractor (Kone) was called in on 30 Dec. Fault traced to a worn door operator belt. Part replaced. Lift has been running normally since. We have asked Kone to include this lift in the next monthly preventive maintenance visit for a full check.

**2.2 Water Seepage at Basement Carpark Wall**

Recurring seepage at the wall near the ramp entrance. We have engaged a specialist (DampSolve) to do a moisture survey. Their report is expected by 15 Jan. Based on their preliminary verbal feedback, the issue appears to be related to groundwater pressure rather than a burst pipe. We have informed the adjacent commercial unit owner (ground floor) as a courtesy since the seepage is on the party wall. No cost incurred yet beyond the survey fee.

**2.3 Gate Barrier at Side Entrance**

The side entrance gate barrier arm was damaged on 26 Dec when a delivery van reversed into it. The driver’s company has admitted liability and their insurer has been notified. We have obtained a quotation for replacement (SGD 1,250) and are waiting for the insurer to confirm. In the meantime, we have manually propped the arm up so the entrance remains usable. The security post has been briefed to monitor the entrance more closely.
